Observations:
- The output bias b3 reads as a per-pixel mean image. As a 12×12 map it is a dark frame (border values ≈ −0.40…−0.60, e.g. b3[0]=−0.551, b3[11]=−0.605, b3[131]=−0.586, b3[142]=−0.428…−0.571) with a large dim/bright region in the middle: central pixels sit near 0 to +0.18, peaking around the lower middle (b3[66]=+0.182 at (row5,col6), +0.122 at (row5,col7), +0.115 at (row6,col5), +0.106 at (row4,col7), +0.098 at (row6,col8), +0.096 at (row7,col3)). So the "average training image" is a lumpy, roughly rounded bright patch spanning roughly rows 2–8, columns 2–9 on a dark background.
- Several hidden-to-pixel weights are purely structural: W3 row 7 (b2[7]=0.680, so this unit is normally active) is ≈ −0.11…−0.20 at every border pixel and positive (+0.02…+0.17) only in the central block (e.g. +0.174 at pixel 65, +0.125 at pixel 75, +0.174 at pixel 53 area) — literally a "dark frame + central blob" template. Rows 9, 10, 14, 21 of W3 are broad negative (~−0.05…−0.10) everywhere, i.e. they only darken the background further.
- Several other W3 units are "content" units with big localized positive patches (~0.35–0.58): row 1 bright at rows 7–9, cols 1–3 (0.538, 0.515, 0.389); row 2 bright at rows 3–6, cols 6–9 (0.427, 0.385); row 19 bright at rows 1–3, cols 4–8 (0.507, 0.503, 0.408); row 25 bright at rows 1–5, cols 0–3 (0.577, 0.552, 0.539); row 35 bright at rows 7–9 cols 0–1 and row 8 cols 9–11 (0.582, 0.525). These are distinct locations/variants, so individual samples differ in where/what the central bright content looks like, but all variants stay inside the same central area.
- W1 shows border pixels (rows 0–13 of W1, and the bottom border rows) have only tiny weights (~0.01–0.03: e.g. row 9 of W1 max ≈ 0.019), while central rows have weights up to ~0.1–0.45 (e.g. W1 row 16 has 0.402 at unit 9, row 31 has 0.437). The network literally doesn't look at the outer frame — it is always background there.
- The time encoding rows (W1 rows 156–157, weights of magnitude 0.3–1.5, e.g. row 157: 0.563, −1.018, 0.983, 1.335, …) strongly gate hidden units on cos(t·f5), which runs from +1 (t=0) to ≈−1 (t≈999). So the model behaves very differently at high noise (coarse mean-like prediction) and low noise (structure refinement), which is the normal diffusion behavior; there is no degenerate "always output the mean" shortcut.

Reasoning:
What is ruled out: no checkerboard/stripe textures (no alternating-sign pixel patterns in W3 rows reaching the borders), no full-frame content (border pixels have near-zero W1 input weights and strongly negative output weights), and no edges-to-edge objects (the brightest b3 values and all large W3 patches are confined to rows 1–10, cols 0–10 with the frame at −0.5…−0.6). What fits: a dataset of dark-background images whose content is a soft bright patch (or a few patches) occupying the central ~6×6 to 8×8 area. The bias map is exactly the average of such images blurred together; individual samples then differ in which of the localized "content" units activate, i.e. the blob shifts/changes shape slightly (toward left rows 1–5, top rows 1–3, right rows 3–6, or bottom rows 7–9), but every sample keeps the same layout: black 1–2-pixel frame, gray-ish dim surround, bright center. Generation will produce near mean-like images at every step because the dominant structure (b3 + the frame/blob unit 7) is t-independent; the variant units only modulate details, so samples will look similar to each other.

Images:
Each sample: a black border (outermost ring, and much of row 1 and row 10), with a soft white/light-gray rounded blob filling the middle of the image (roughly a disk/rounded square of diameter ~6–7 pixels centered slightly at rows 4–6). The blob's brightest point sits a bit right-of/below center; the edges of the blob fade gradually into gray. Between samples the blob shifts slightly (sometimes bulging to the upper area, sometimes to the lower-left) but never touches the frame.

Observations: The strongest signal in this network is in the output layer, and it is best read as "templates + a mean image."

- **b3 already looks like a picture.** Arranged as a 12×12 grid, the output biases are a dark vignette around everything: corners are the most negative (component (0,0)=−0.691, (0,11)=−0.714, (11,0)=−0.626, (11,11)=−0.690), edge mids are −0.3…−0.55, and the **interior hovers near zero with a faint bright core** around rows 4–7, cols 3–8: b3[54]=+0.064, b3[60+6]=+0.093, b3[6·12+5]=+0.102, +0.071, +0.069 nearby. So even with no input, the best single prediction is "black background, slightly lifted middle."

- **Most W3 rows are noise (~±0.02), but roughly 15–20 units carry strong, localized, single-pixel-scale templates.** Examples:
  - Unit 0: a positive **vertical stroke column at column 4**, rows 4–7: +0.300, +0.534, +0.352, +0.151 (peak exactly at pixel (5,4)), also +0.145 at (1,4), +0.112/+0.142 at (9,3)/(9,4), with **negative flanks** just left of it: −0.188, −0.171 at (5,1)/(5,2), −0.137/−0.121 at (6,1)/(6,2). Center-on-surround: brighten a 1‑px stroke, darken its background.
  - Unit 5: strong negatives along **cols 5–6, rows 2–7** (−0.220 at (2,5), −0.367 at (4,6), −0.295 at (6,6)) with bright columns alongside (+0.106…+0.217 around (3,9)–(3,10), +0.11…0.13 cols 1–4).
  - Unit 1: positive cluster **upper-middle-right** (+0.165 at (1,8), +0.160 at (2,8), +0.140 at (3,7), +0.182 at (4,7)) and deep negatives at (6,6…9) down to −0.505 at (6,8) — ink that appears high but never appears below it.
  - Unit 2: big dark blob at (9,3…9), peak −0.446 at (9,6). Unit ~31: dark blob rows 5–7, cols 1–7, peak −0.563 at (6,4).
  - Unit 7: almost the whole row negative (−0.08…−0.34, capping at −0.29…−0.34 across row 11) with a small positive lobe at (3,4)–(4,5) (+0.123, +0.164, +0.200 at (5,4)) — a strong background-darkener with one bright exception.
  - One unit has a broad **top band**: row 1 ≈ +0.210…+0.510 across cols 2–10 (peak +0.510), plus +0.44…+0.51 at rows 0–1 — frequent ink near the top-center rows.

- **The time-encoding inputs matter a lot**: W1 rows 144–159 have entries up to ±0.8 for the sin rows (e.g. −0.640, −0.536, −0.556) and up to ±1.4 for a few cos rows (e.g. 1.430, 1.388, 1.357), so template choice/mixing is strongly t-conditioned — coarse templates influence early, pixel-sharp stroke templates bite at low t.

Reasoning: x₀̂'s dominant term is b3, i.e. the training-set mean: black bordered image with a modestly lifted center. That rules out flat/gray images, noise images, large filled shapes or fixed-position bright objects (the center would then be strongly positive), and photographic/grayscale scenes (structure is stroke-like and sparse, and clipping to [−1,1] plus the sharp ±0.5 single-pixel templates indicate near-binary ink). The units are center-on-surround and bar/flank detectors tuned to precise pixel positions in the middle band of the image (cols ~1–9, rows ~1–10), both "brighten this stroke" and "never ink here" types, with several different stroke positions/topologies across units. That is the signature of a set of **small glyph-like white drawings — digit/character-like strokes** — white ink of 1–2 px width confined to the central ~8×8 area on a black, corner-vignetted background, with the specific stroke layout varying between samples (vertical strokes near cols 4–6, tops/upper-right hooks, mid bands, tails). Images are not all identical and not centered disks; they are a family of sparse stroke patterns.

Images: Black background throughout, darkest at the four corners. In the central window (roughly rows 1–10, cols 2–9) a small handwritten-style glyph made of white strokes 1–2 pixels wide — vertical bar–like strokes near the middle columns, sometimes with a top flag/serif, hooks, or small horizontal bands; different samples give different digit-like shapes.

Observations:
- **The output bias b3 is the strongest clue.** Read as a 12×12 grid (pixel j = row 12*r + c), it is a picture of the model's *average* clean image. Every border pixel is strongly negative (corners: −0.535, −0.532, −0.510, −0.504, −0.500, −0.456…; the entire top row and bottom row are ≈ −0.15…−0.55). The interior is much brighter, peaking around rows 5–8, cols 3–8: −0.013 at (2,5), 0.069 at (7,3), 0.063 at (5,7), 0.049 at (5,3), 0.046 at (6,3), 0.040 at (8,3). So the average training image is a **dark background with one bright central region**.
- **The boundary of the bright region tapers in every direction** (row 2 is bright only around cols 5–8, row 3 covers cols ~3–8, rows 4–8 reach cols ~2–9, rows 9–10 fade back), while column 11 and column 0 stay uniformly dark at heights 3–8 (−0.53/−0.51/−0.41 vs. −0.08/0.05 in mid-columns). Curved tapering + uniformly dark extreme corners = a **round blob, not a square or full-height shape**.
- **W3 holds local edge filters aimed exactly at that boundary.** Row 0 has an isolated diagonal edge pattern: positives along (2,7), (3,6), (4,6), (5,5), (6,5) (0.163, 0.191, 0.318, 0.193, 0.215) with negatives just above (−0.185, −0.339, −0.222). Row 8 is an edge of the opposite orientation: positives along (2,6), (3,7), (4,7), (5,8), (6,8), (7,9), (8,10) (0.122, 0.282, 0.360, 0.436, 0.314, 0.287). Row 1 is a horizontal-edge filter (positives band rows 2–3 cols 5–9: 0.106, 0.198, 0.163; strong negatives at row 4 cols 5–10: −0.350, −0.354, −0.389, −0.384). Edge filters in many orientations at the rim of the blob are what you need for a **curved boundary** — a square would need only two orientations, and a cross/line would need a thin bright skeleton instead of a filled patch.
- **Filling of the interior:** row 12 of W3 is a broad positive kernel centered at lower-middle (…0.159, 0.368, **0.686**, 0.185… at pixels 115–117; 0.324 at 116?/95, 0.422 at 103, 0.232 at 79) — a "blob amplifier" for the disc's core.
- **The background is actively forced to black:** several W3 rows are essentially uniform and negative across all 144 pixels (row 15 ≈ −0.05…−0.09 everywhere; row 33 ≈ −0.05…−0.14; row 56 ≈ −0.05…−0.10; row 63 ≈ −0.07…−0.17; similar rows 19, 22, 23, 31, 53), and b3 starts at ≈ −0.4 everywhere. Together these drive non-object pixels toward −1.
- **Time is genuinely used through the Fourier features:** W1 rows 144–159 include very strong entries into a few units (e.g., row 153 → unit 1: −1.210, unit 4: 1.202, unit 5: 1.353, unit 16: 1.386, unit 19: 0.894, unit 38: 1.441; row 146: −0.819 at unit 2, −0.782/−0.717…), so the model can switch between "coarse blob fill" at high t and "edge refinement" at low t. Also, some first-layer units are pegged to specific pixels (e.g., pixel 18 → unit 19 with 0.389; pixel 28 → unit 28 with 0.351; pixel 14 → unit 14 with 0.396/0.421) — pixel-local anchors for the boundary region, again centered, not at the frame corners.

Reasoning:
- The bias is the learned prior mean of x₀, so it directly sketches the average training image: **one contiguous bright form centered in the frame on an all-dark background**. Only one bright cluster appears in b3, so the images contain **a single object**, not several.
- Center pixels are the brightest b3 values, so the object is a **filled** form, not an outline or ring (a ring would make the very center dark, like −0.5, but (5..8, 3) are near 0 to +0.07).
- No straight full-height/full-width bright column or bright row appears in the mean, and the corner/edge brightness changes with distance to the center (e.g., −0.535 at (3,0) vs −0.077 at (4,2) vs 0.049 at (5,3)), which is the signature of a **circular boundary**. A square, cross, triangle or line is ruled out; symmetric digits/letters are unlikely (all four sides taper the same way, no interior strokes).
- The mean is a bit soft/lower-left heavy, suggesting the training collection consists of this disc with slight positional/scale variation; generated samples will all show essentially the same thing: one white filled circle on black.

Images: Every generated image shows a single **white filled circle** (a "dot"/disc), roughly 7–8 pixels across, centered in the 12×12 frame (slightly toward the lower middle), on a solid black background. Sample-to-sample variation is small: only the exact rim position of the circle wobbles a little.
